question: A 12-year-old boy is assessed during a health checkup. He shows pubic hair that is darker, curlier, and covers a wider area than adult-like hair, but the genitalia are only slightly enlarged with scrotal reddening. According to Tanner/SMR staging, which stage does this correspond to?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Stage 1 is the pre-pubertal state with no pubic hair and childhood-size genitalia.

answers.text: Tanner Stage 2 — first visible pubic hair, slight genital enlargement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Stage 2 shows sparse, lightly pigmented, straight pubic hair and initial scrotal reddening — not curly or widely spread hair.

answers.text: Tanner Stage 3 — darker, curlier pubic hair spreading over pubic area; genitalia enlarging

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Stage 3 is characterised by darker, curlier pubic hair spreading across the pubic region, with enlargement of the penis in length and further growth of the testes and scrotum.

answers.text: Tanner Stage 4 — adult-type hair but not extending to thighs; adult-size genitalia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Stage 4 shows adult-type curly hair that does not yet extend to the medial thighs, and genitalia are near adult size — more advanced than described.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Tanner/SMR staging sequence carefully — the key discriminators are pubic-hair texture, distribution, and genital size. SMR Stage 3 is the transition stage where hair becomes clearly adult-type in quality but not yet in distribution.
Well done. SMR Stage 3 = darker, curlier pubic hair spreading over the pubic triangle with continued genital growth. Onset of gynecomastia in boys also commonly occurs at Stage 3.
